Welcome to the planets website!

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

# Nearest stars to Earth with distance in light-years
stars <- tibble(
  star = c("Earth (Sun)", "Proxima Centauri", "Alpha Centauri A", "Barnard's Star", 
           "Wolf 359", "Lalande 21185", "Sirius", "Luyten 726-8", "Ross 154"),
  dist_ly = c(0, 4.25, 4.37, 5.96, 7.86, 8.31, 8.66, 8.73, 9.70),
  angle_deg = c(0, 45, 60, 110, 160, 200, 240, 290, 330)
) |> 
  # Convert polar coordinates (distance and angle) to 2D x and y coordinates
  mutate(
    x = dist_ly * cos(angle_deg * pi / 180),
    y = dist_ly * sin(angle_deg * pi / 180)
  )

ggplot(stars, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  # Dashed circles representing 5 and 10 light-year distances from Earth
  annotate("path",
    x = 5 * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)),
    y = 5 * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)),
    color = "gray75", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  annotate("path",
    x = 10 * cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)),
    y = 10 * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)),
    color = "gray75", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 5.3, label = "5 light-years", color = "gray50", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 10.3, label = "10 light-years", color = "gray50", size = 3) +
  # Plot Earth and stars
  geom_point(aes(color = (star == "Earth (Sun)")), size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = star), vjust = -1, size = 3.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "blue", "FALSE" = "darkorange"), guide = "none") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(
    title = "Nearby Stars Relative to Earth",
    subtitle = "Distances measured in light-years with Earth at the center",
    x = "Light-Years",
    y = "Light-Years"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
